title: Strategy search: every rule we could think of, on five seasons
question: Study the data we already have to find a strategy (position sizing, when to cash out...) that would have had positive ROI. I know this can be overfitting but we can try first.
rule: Every rule tried is counted: the raw model's best side at an edge of 0, 5, 12 or 20%, Blend Lean at z 0.5, 1 or 2, or every side, in 1X2, draw no bet, Asian handicap and over/under 2.5 at Pinnacle's early price, with up to two filters (league, price band, edge or z band, driver, side, favourite, day, kickoff slot, strength gap), plus line-movement rules at the close. A rule passes only if its CLV range is above 0 on 300+ bets and it beats the best a no-skill search would find by luck (p < 0.05). 2024/25 onward is locked away for any finalist.
verdict_text: No strategy found. 11,857 rules tried; the best beat the closing price by +1.3% on 320 bets, but a search with no skill finds one that good 94% of the time. Only 2% of the large rules beat the close at all, against about half if prices were beatable by chance.

notes: Every number is from 2019/20 to 2023/24 (seasons where Pinnacle's early and closing prices both cover 90% of matches). 2024/25 onward was never read.
CLV is the entry price against Pinnacle's margin-free close; ROI is per $1. Ranges resample matches (2,000 draws).
Line-movement rules are decided at the close, so they have no CLV and are judged on ROI only; none can be a finalist.
The curve is the best rule by CLV: it beat the close but still lost or barely broke even, and the search's luck check says rules like it turn up by chance.
Cashing out (the exits) was tested separately on the comeback sample: a fair cash-out never changes the average return, and a real one costs money.
